hard_break_spaces.description: With a value above 0, that many spaces or more at the end of a line that the next non-blank line follows are a hard line break and not reported (Markdown: 2).

ignore_kinds.description: Kinds of tokens whose trailing white space is not reported (the code of a fence).

no-typename-prefix.description: Reports a field of an object or interface type that starts with the name of the type (`type User { userId: ID }`); case is ignored.

no-undefined-alias.description: Reports an alias that names an anchor not defined earlier in the same document, on the alias.

no-unexpected-multiline.description: Reports a line that begins with `(`, `[` or a template literal right after a line that ends an expression, where the two lines are one expression: `var d = a` followed by `(b);` calls `a(b)`.

no-unit-return.description: Reports a function with a block body that declares `: Unit` as its return type.

no-unknown-elements.description: Reports an element name that HTML does not define, custom elements (`<my-element>`) included.

no-unknown-style-directive-property.description: Reports a `style:` directive that names a property CSS does not know (`style:marginLeft`).

no-unnecessary-type-constraint.description: Reports a type parameter constrained to `any` or `unknown` (`<T extends unknown>`, also with a default).

no-unneeded-base-prefix.description: Reports `base.M()` or `base[i]` where the type does not override the member, so `this` binds to the same one.

no-unneeded-ternary.description: Reports a conditional expression whose two arms are both boolean literals: `a ? true : false` (the same as `!!a`), `a ? false : true` (`!a`), and `a ? true : true`.

no-unsafe-finally.description: Reports `return`, `throw`, and a `break` or `continue` that leaves the `finally` block, written in a `finally`.

no-unsafe-function-type.description: Reports the global type `Function` used as a type, as an `interface ... extends` target and as an `implements` target.

no-unsafe-negation.description: Reports `!a in b` and `!a instanceof B`, where the `!` is written without parentheses on the left operand.

no-unset-hookable-property.description: Reports `unset($this->name)` of a property the class declares when a subclass could give the property a hook (PHP 8.4): the class is not final and the property is not private, final, static or readonly.

no-unused-anchors.description: Reports an anchor that no alias refers to.

no-use-v-else-with-v-for.description: Reports an element that has `v-else` and `v-for` together.

no-use-v-if-with-v-for.description: Reports an element that has `v-if` and `v-for` together.

no-useless-catch.description: Reports a `catch` clause whose only statement is `throw` of the caught error, as in `catch (e) { throw e; }`.

no-useless-children-snippet.description: Reports a `{#snippet children()}` with no parameters inside a component.

no-useless-escape.description: Reports a backslash before a character that needs no escape, in a string (`'\d'`), a template literal or a regex literal (`/\-/`, `/\_/`).

no-useless-expression.description: Reports an expression statement whose value is thrown away and that has no effect of its own: a name, a literal, a member access or an operator expression (`x + y;`, `x.y;`, `-x;`, `x ? y : z;`).

no-v-for-template-key-on-child.description: Reports a `:key` on a child of a `<template v-for>`.

no-var.description: Reports a `var` declaration (also `declare var` in TypeScript).

no-void-end-tag.description: Reports an end tag of a void element (`</br>`, `</img>`).

no-wildcard-imports.description: Reports an import of every name of a package or module (`import a.b.*;` in Java and Kotlin, `from a import *` in Python, `import .

wildcard_aliases.description: The aliases that bring in every name of the imported package

no-wrapper-object-types.description: Reports the global types `BigInt`, `Boolean`, `Number`, `Object`, `String` and `Symbol` used as type names.

none-comparison.description: Reports a comparison of a value to `None` with `==` or `!=`.

not-in-test.description: Reports a membership test negated in front of the expression: `not a in b`.

not-is-test.description: Reports an identity test negated in front of the expression: `not a is b`.

npm-pin-versions.description: Reports an `npm install` (also `npm i` and `npm add`) of a package without a version: `express` instead of `express@4.18.2`, `@scope/name` instead of `@scope/name@1.2.0`.

null-comparison-side.description: Reports a `-eq` or `-ne` comparison (or a case variant, as `-ceq`) with `$null` on the right.

number-max-precision.description: Reports a number with more decimal places than the `max` option.

max.description: The most decimal places a number may have.

numeric-user-id.description: Reports a `USER` whose user is a name instead of a number (`USER app`, `USER app:1000`).

oneof-lower-snake-case.description: Reports a oneof name that is not lower_snake_case.

open-file-without-with.description: Reports a call of `open` or `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile` and the like that is not the context of a `with`, is not returned and is not given to `enter_context`.

optional-annotation.description: Reports a `typing.Optional[...]` subscript when the `target_version` has `X | Y` (3.10 and later).

os-error-alias.description: Reports `EnvironmentError`, `IOError`, `WindowsError`, `mmap.error`, `os.error`, `select.error` or `socket.error` in an `except` clause or a `raise`.

outdated-action.description: Reports a step that uses a popular action at a version whose runner (the Node version it runs on) is retired, from a list of actions kept with the rule.

outdated-version-block.description: Reports a test of `sys.version_info` against a version older than the `target_version`, or of `sys.version_info[0]` against a number.

package-comment-form.description: Reports a package comment whose first line does not start with `Package` and the name of the package.

package-defined.description: Reports a file without a `package` statement.

package-lower-snake-case.description: Reports a package whose components are not lower_snake_case.

package-name.description: Reports a package whose name has an uppercase letter or an underscore.

package-version-suffix.description: Reports a package whose last component is not `v1`, `v1test...`, `v1alpha1`, `v1beta1` or `v1p1alpha1` (`v1beta` too).

parameter-assignment.description: Reports an assignment to a parameter of a method.

parameter-list-wrapping.description: Reports a parameter list that the formatter would wrap or join differently.

parentheses-as-grouped-expression.description: Reports a space between a method name and a `(` that holds its only argument (`puts (x)`).

percent-format-expected-mapping.description: Reports a `%` format that has named placeholders (`%(a)s`) applied to a tuple, list or set.

percent-format-expected-sequence.description: Reports a `%` format that has several positional placeholders applied to a dict.

percent-format-extra-named-arguments.description: Reports a `%` format applied to a dict that has keys that no placeholder names.

percent-format-invalid-format.description: Reports a `"..." % x` whose format string does not parse, such as a `%` at the end of the string.

percent-format-missing-argument.description: Reports a `%` format with named placeholders that the dict does not have.

percent-format-mixed-positional-and-name.description: Reports a `%` format that has both positional placeholders (`%s`) and named ones (`%(a)s`).

percent-format-positional-count-mismatch.description: Reports a `%` format whose number of placeholders differs from the number of values in the tuple.

percent-format-star-requires-sequence.description: Reports a `%` format with a `*` width or precision applied to a dict.

percent-format-unsupported-format-charac.description: Reports a `%` format with a conversion character that Python does not know, as in `"%z" % x`.

phony-declared.description: Reports a target with no recipe that is not declared `.PHONY`.

pip-pin-versions.description: Reports a `pip install` (also `pip3`, `pip3.12`) of a package without a version.

pipefail-shell.description: Reports a `RUN` with a pipe (`a | b`) in a stage whose `SHELL` does not set `pipefail`.

possible-null-dereference.description: Reports a member or element access on an expression that the nullable analysis says may be null.

post-condition-loop.description: Reports `begin ... end while cond` and `begin ... end until cond`.

prefer-as-const.description: Reports a literal type that only repeats the literal it is given: `let a: 'a' = 'a'`, `'a' as 'a'` and `<'a'>'a'`.

prefer-const.description: Reports a `let` variable that is assigned once and could be a `const`: the single write is its initializer, a `for-in` or `for-of` head, or the first assignment statement in the same block as the declaration.

prefer-control-flow.description: Reports a `*ngIf` or `*ngFor` attribute and a `[ngSwitch]` binding: the directives that the `@if`, `@for` and `@switch` blocks of Angular 17 replace.

prefer-native-element.description: Reports a `role` that a native element already has (`main`, `navigation`, `button`, `list`, ...) when it is on an element that is not that one (`<div role="main">`, `<a role="button">`).

prefer-rest-params.description: Reports `arguments` used in an ordinary function, except as the object of a member read by name (`arguments.length`).

prefer-spread.description: Reports `f.apply(undefined, args)`, `f.apply(null, args)`, `o.m.apply(o, args)` and `o['m'].apply(o, args)`, where the first argument is `null`, `undefined`, or the same object that the method is read from.

prefer-tbody.description: Reports a `<tr>` that is directly in a `<table>`.

printf-string-formatting.description: Reports a `"..." % x` whose format string and values pair up: a tuple with as many values as placeholders, a dict for named fields, or one value for one placeholder.

printf-variable-format.description: Reports a `printf` whose format string contains an expansion and no `%`.

process-block-for-pipeline.description: Reports a function or script block with a parameter that has `ValueFromPipeline` or `ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName` and no `process` block.

property-allowed-list.description: Reports a property that is not in the `list` option (names, or `/regex/`).

property-disallowed-list.description: Reports a property that is in the `list` option (names, or `/regex/`).

property-naming.description: Reports a property whose name does not match the expression set for its kind: a `const val` is in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; top-level and object properties may also be written as constants; a backing property may start with `_`; an `override` is not reported.

constants.description: Regular expression the name of a `const val` must match; empty: not checked.

members.description: Regular expression the name of any other property (a member of a class, a local) must match.

overridden.description: Regular expression the name of an `override` property must match.

singleton_members.description: Regular expression the name of a property of an object must match.

top_level.description: Regular expression the name of a top-level property must match.

property-no-deprecated.description: Reports a deprecated property (`clip`, `word-wrap`, `grid-gap`, the `box-*` properties of the old flexbox, ...).

property-no-unknown.description: Reports a property that no CSS specification lists.

property-no-vendor-prefix.description: Reports a vendor-prefixed property that has a standard property (`-webkit-transition`).

property-summary-matches-accessors.description: Reports a property summary that does not start with "Gets", "Sets" or "Gets or sets" as the accessors that are reachable from outside the type say; for `bool` properties "Gets a value indicating whether" and the like.

property-summary-omits-restricted-access.description: Reports a property summary that says "Gets or sets" while one of the accessors is not reachable from outside the type (`private set`, `internal get` on a public property).

qualify-instance-members.description: Reports a field, property, method or event of the containing type that is used by its simple name.

qualify-namespace-usings.description: Reports a `using` directive inside a namespace whose name is not written fully qualified, so that it resolves relative to the enclosing namespace.

quote-array-element.description: Reports an unquoted `$var` or `${var}` among the elements of an array assignment, as in `arr=($x y)`.

quote-at-expansion.description: Reports an unquoted `$@` or `${array[@]}` in the arguments of a command.

quote-command-substitution.description: Reports an unquoted `$(...)` or backtick substitution in the arguments of a command.

quote-in-quotes.description: Reports a word made of two double-quoted strings with unquoted text between them, where a quoted part has a blank, as in `"say "hi" now"`.

quote-star-expansion.description: Reports an unquoted `$*` or `${array[*]}` in the arguments of a command.

quote-variable.description: Reports an unquoted `$var` or `${var}` in the arguments of a command.

quoted-annotation.description: Reports a quoted name in a parameter, return or variable annotation when the `target_version` does not evaluate annotations at definition (3.14 and later).

quoted-strings.description: Reports strings that are quoted or unquoted against the rule you set with `required`: `always` wants quotes on every string, `only_when_needed` reports quotes that change nothing (unless `extra_allowed` matches) and plain strings that `extra_required` matches, `optional` only the latter.

allow_quoted_quotes.description: Accept the other quote type when the string contains the wanted quote.

extra_allowed.description: Regular expressions; a string they match may be quoted with `only_when_needed`.

extra_required.description: Regular expressions; a string they match (searched in the value) must be quoted even with `optional` or `only_when_needed`.

quote_type.description: The quotes to use. `consistent`: the first quoted string of the file decides.

required.description: `always`: every string is quoted. `optional`: quotes are free, but must be of `quote_type`. `only_when_needed`: quotes only where the string would otherwise read as something else.

raise-not-implemented.description: Reports a `raise` of `NotImplemented`, with or without a call.

raise-without-from-inside-except.description: Reports a `raise` of an exception inside an `except` clause without `from`.

range.description: `for k, _ := range x`: the second value is the blank identifier, so `for k := range x` says the same.

receiver-name-consistent.description: The methods of a type declared in one file name their receiver the same.

receiver-naming.description: The name of a method's receiver is `_`, `this` or `self`: a receiver is named by a short form of its type, and left out when the method does not use it.

receivers.description: A regular expression the receiver name must match; one that starts with `!` is one it must not match. Empty: not checked.

redeclared-variable.description: Reports a name declared again in the same scope (`var` twice, a `var` and a parameter, two functions).

redefines-builtin-id.description: Reports a variable, constant, function, parameter, named result or type parameter that has the name of a predeclared identifier (`len`, `new`, `string`, `nil`, `max`, ...); a name on the left of an assignment counts too.

assigned_by.description: Grammar kinds of statements whose left-side names are reported too (`len = 1`, `max += 1`).

except_parents.description: Grammar kinds whose direct declarations are left out (a receiver).

kinds.description: The declarations that are checked (empty: all).

redundant-pattern.description: Reports a `foo/` or `/foo` pattern that follows a plain `foo`, with no `!` pattern between them: a name pattern already matches files and directories called `foo` at every level.

redundant-return-type.description: Removes a return type that the language gives every function with a block body anyway (`fun f(): Unit { }` in Kotlin; the types come from the option `redundant_return_types`).

redundant-string-coercion.description: Reports `to_s` on the last expression of a `#{...}` and on an argument of `puts`, `print` or `warn`.

redundant-tuple-in-exception-handler.description: Reports an `except` clause that names a tuple of one exception, `except (E,):`.

regex-flag-alias.description: Reports `re.A`, `re.I`, `re.L`, `re.M`, `re.S`, `re.U` and `re.X`, the short names of `re.ASCII`, `re.IGNORECASE`, `re.LOCALE`, `re.MULTILINE`, `re.DOTALL`, `re.UNICODE` and `re.VERBOSE`.

remove-unused-usings.description: Reports a `using` directive that nothing in the file needs.

require-default-prop.description: Reports a prop that is not required, has no `default` and is not a `Boolean` (`defineProps({ a: String })`).

require-each-key.description: Reports an `{#each}` block with no key (`{#each items as item}`).

require-for-track.description: Reports an `@for` block with no `track` expression.

require-li-container.description: Reports an `<li>` whose parent is not a list (`<ul>`, `<ol>` or `<menu>`).

require-prop-types.description: Reports a prop in the array form (`defineProps(['a'])`), and an object with no `type` or `validator`.

require-sri.description: Reports a `<script src>` and a `<link rel="stylesheet" href>` with no `integrity` attribute.

require-yield.description: Reports a generator (`function*`, a generator method, `async function*`) that has statements but no `yield`.

required-providers.description: Reports a provider that a `resource`, `data` or `provider` block uses and that no `required_providers` entry of the module names, on the last such block of the provider, and a `required_providers` entry without a `version`.

required-version.description: Reports a module none of whose `terraform` blocks sets `required_version`, on the `terraform` block, or on the start of `main.tf` when the module has no such block.

return-in-void-context.description: Reports `return value` in `initialize` or a setter method, whose result is ignored.

return-outside-function.description: Reports a `return` that is not inside a function.

root-in-section.description: Reports a `root` property inside a section.

rpc-pascal-case.description: Reports an rpc name that is not PascalCase.

rpc-request-response-unique.description: Reports an rpc whose request or response type is also the request or response type of another rpc of the project.

rpc-request-standard-name.description: Reports an rpc whose request type is not named `<Rpc>Request` or `<Service><Rpc>Request`.

rpc-response-standard-name.description: Reports an rpc whose response type is not named `<Rpc>Response` or `<Service><Rpc>Response`.

rpm-pin-versions.description: Reports a `yum install`, `dnf install` or `microdnf install` of a package without a version.

rule-empty-line-before.description: Reports a rule whose block spans several lines and has no empty line before it.

script-injection.description: Reports an expression in a `run` script that reads text that an attacker can choose, such as the title or body of an issue or pull request, a branch name or a commit message.

script-type.description: Reports a `<script>` whose `type` is a JavaScript MIME type (`text/javascript`, `application/javascript`, ...) or empty.

selection-set-depth.description: Reports an operation or fragment that nests selection sets deeper than the `max` option allows.

max.description: The deepest allowed nesting; the operation's own selection set is level 1.

selector-anb-no-unmatchable.description: Reports an `:nth-child()` and the like whose `An+B` can never match (`0`, `0n`, `-n`, `-2n-1`).

selector-attribute-name-disallowed-list.description: Reports an attribute selector whose name is in the `list` option.

list.description: The disallowed attribute names: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-attribute-operator-allowed-list.description: Reports an attribute selector operator that is not in the `list` option.

selector-attribute-operator-disallowed-l.description: Reports an attribute selector operator that is in the `list` option.

selector-attribute-quotes.description: Reports an attribute selector whose value is not quoted (`[a=b]`).

selector-class-pattern.description: Reports a class selector whose name does not match the `pattern` option (a regex).

pattern.description: The regex a class name must match.

selector-combinator-allowed-list.description: Reports a combinator (`>`, `+`, `~`, or a space for the descendant combinator) that is not in the `list` option.

selector-combinator-disallowed-list.description: Reports a combinator (`>`, `+`, `~`, or a space for the descendant combinator) that is in the `list` option.

selector-disallowed-list.description: Reports a rule whose selector list, with whitespace collapsed, is in the `list` option (selectors, or `/regex/`).

selector-id-pattern.description: Reports an id selector whose name does not match the `pattern` option (a regex).

pattern.description: The regex an id name must match.

selector-max-attribute.description: Reports a selector with more attribute selectors than the `max` option.

max.description: The most attribute selectors a selector may have.

selector-max-class.description: Reports a selector with more class selectors than the `max` option; classes inside `:not()` and the like count.

max.description: The most classes a selector may have.

selector-max-combinators.description: Reports a selector with more combinators than the `max` option; a space between two compound selectors counts.

max.description: The most combinators a selector may have.

selector-max-compound-selectors.description: Reports a selector with more compound selectors (parts between combinators) than the `max` option.

max.description: The most compound selectors a selector may have.

selector-max-id.description: Reports a selector with more id selectors than the `max` option.

max.description: The most ids a selector may have.

selector-max-pseudo-class.description: Reports a selector with more pseudo-classes than the `max` option.

max.description: The most pseudo-classes a selector may have.

selector-max-type.description: Reports a selector with more type selectors than the `max` option.

max.description: The most type selectors a selector may have.

selector-max-universal.description: Reports a selector with more `*` than the `max` option.

max.description: The most universal selectors a selector may have.

selector-no-deprecated.description: Reports a deprecated pseudo-class, pseudo-element or HTML or SVG element used as a type selector (`center {}`).

selector-no-qualifying-type.description: Reports a type selector in the same compound as a class, id or attribute selector (`ul.nav`).

selector-no-vendor-prefix.description: Reports a vendor-prefixed pseudo-class or pseudo-element that has a standard one (`::-moz-selection`).

selector-pseudo-class-allowed-list.description: Reports a pseudo-class that is not in the `list` option.

list.description: The allowed pseudo-classes, without `:`: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-pseudo-class-disallowed-list.description: Reports a pseudo-class that is in the `list` option.

list.description: The disallowed pseudo-classes, without `:`: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-pseudo-class-no-unknown.description: Reports a pseudo-class that is not a CSS one.

selector-pseudo-element-allowed-list.description: Reports a pseudo-element that is not in the `list` option.

list.description: The allowed pseudo-elements, without colons: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation.description: Reports `:before`, `:after`, `:first-line` or `:first-letter` written with one colon.

selector-pseudo-element-disallowed-list.description: Reports a pseudo-element that is in the `list` option.

list.description: The disallowed pseudo-elements, without colons: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-pseudo-element-no-unknown.description: Reports a pseudo-element that is not a CSS one.

selector-type-case.description: Reports a type selector with capitals (`A {}`).

selector-type-no-unknown.description: Reports a type selector that is not an HTML, SVG or MathML element; custom elements are accepted.

self-alias.description: Reports an alias that repeats the name it is given to, as in `a AS a`.

separate-attributes.description: Reports an attribute list with several attributes: `[A, B]` is `[A]` and `[B]`.

separate-field-declarations.description: Reports a declaration of several fields or events (`int a, b;`), which becomes `int a;` and `int b;`, each with the attributes, modifiers and type of the original.

service-pascal-case.description: Reports a service name that is not PascalCase.

service-suffix.description: Reports a service whose name does not end in `Service`.

set-attr-with-constant.description: Reports a statement `setattr(x, "name", v)` with a literal name that is a valid identifier.

shadowed-variable.description: Reports a variable, parameter or function with the name of one declared in a scope around it.

kinds.description: The declarations that are checked for shadowing something (empty: all).

shorthand-attribute.description: Reports `name={name}` where the shorthand `{name}` would do.

shorthand-directive.description: Reports `bind:name={name}`, `class:name={name}` and `style:name={name}` where the shorthand (`bind:name`) would do.

shorthand-property-no-redundant-values.description: Reports a `margin`, `padding`, `border-color`, `border-style`, `border-width` or `border-radius` with two, three or four values that repeat (`1px 1px` is `1px`).

single-class-per-file.description: Reports a class or record that comes after the first one in a file: more parts of the first class (when it is partial) are not reported.

single-cmd.description: Reports each `CMD` after the first one in the same stage.

single-entrypoint.description: Reports each `ENTRYPOINT` after the first one in the same stage.

single-healthcheck.description: Reports each `HEALTHCHECK` after the first one in the same stage, `HEALTHCHECK NONE` included.

single-namespace-per-file.description: Reports a namespace that comes after the first one in a file; nested namespaces are reported too.

single-title.description: Reports a second or later top-level heading (`# Title`) in a document.

singular-nouns.description: Reports a function named `Verb-Nouns` whose noun ends in `s`.

sorted-array-values.description: Reports the items of a sequence that are not in order, for sequences of only strings or only numbers (ascending by default; numbers compare as numbers).

blank_line_groups.description: Sort each run of entries between blank lines on its own.

compare.description: `ordinal` (code points), `case_insensitive`, or `natural` (digit runs compare as numbers: `a2` before `a10`).

min_values.description: Sequences with fewer items are not checked.

path_patterns.description: Regular expressions; only mappings (sequences) whose key path matches one are checked. The path is `a.b[0].c` (`["odd key"]` for keys that are not identifiers), empty for the root; none listed means everywhere. A TOML table counts as its header key and an array table is not indexed.

sorted-keys.description: Reports the keys of a mapping that are not in order (alphabetical by default).

blank_line_groups.description: Sort each run of entries between blank lines on its own.

compare.description: `ordinal` (code points), `case_insensitive`, or `natural` (digit runs compare as numbers: `a2` before `a10`).

has_properties.description: Only mappings that have all of these keys are checked.

ignored_keys.description: Regular expressions; matching keys stay where they are and are not compared.

min_keys.description: Mappings with fewer keys are not checked.

order.description: Keys that come first, in this order; the rest follow in the configured order.

path_patterns.description: Regular expressions; only mappings (sequences) whose key path matches one are checked. The path is `a.b[0].c` (`["odd key"]` for keys that are not identifiers), empty for the root; none listed means everywhere. A TOML table counts as its header key and an array table is not indexed.

report.description: Which keys are reported. `moved`: the fewest keys that would have to move (eslint-plugin-jsonc). `misplaced`: every key that sorts before one above it (yamllint).

spaced-html-comment.description: Reports an HTML comment with no space after `<!--` or before `-->` (`<!--text-->`).

special-chars-in-identifier.description: Reports a quoted identifier with a space or another character that is not a letter, a digit or an underscore.

split-command-output.description: Reports an unquoted `$(...)` among the elements of an array assignment, as in `arr=($(cmd))`.

statement-blank-lines.description: Reports more than `max` blank lines (default 1) right before a top-level statement (a direct child of the file that starts its line).

max.description: The longest run of blank lines allowed before a statement.

statement-indent.description: Reports a statement, the closing parenthesis of a multi-line statement or a comment between statements that is not at the column that its block depth gives (depth times `size`, default 2) in a language whose files are a flat list of commands with block words such as `if` and `endif` (CMake).

allow_unindented.description: Accept a token at column 0 whatever its depth.

statement-wrapping.description: Reports a block whose line breaks the formatter would change, such as several statements on one line (`{ a(); b() }`).

static-join.description: Reports `"sep".join([a, b])` where the list or tuple is written out in the call.

string-dot-format-extra-named-arguments.description: Reports a `.format` call with keyword arguments that no field names.

string-dot-format-extra-positional-argum.description: Reports a `.format` call with positional arguments that no field uses.

string-dot-format-invalid-format.description: Reports a `"...".format(...)` call whose string does not parse, such as an unmatched `{` or `}`.

string-dot-format-missing-arguments.description: Reports a `.format` call without an argument for a field of its string.

string-dot-format-mixing-automatic.description: Reports a `.format` string that has both automatic fields (`{}`) and numbered ones (`{0}`).

string-literal-equality.description: Reports `==` or `!=` with a string literal as an operand.

struct-new-override.description: Reports a `Struct.new` member that has the name of a method of `Struct` (`:hash`, `:size`, `:count`).

subprocess-run-without-check.description: Reports a call of `subprocess.run` with no `check` keyword.

superfluous-else.description: An `else` block after an `if` block that ends in `break`, `continue` or `goto`: the code of the `else` can follow the `if`.

supports-should-process.description: Reports a function whose name has the verb `New`, `Set`, `Remove`, `Start`, `Stop`, `Restart`, `Reset` or `Update` and whose text has no `SupportsShouldProcess`, or has `SupportsShouldProcess = $false`.

suppression-justification.description: Reports a `SuppressMessage` attribute whose `Justification` is missing, `null`, empty, blank, or `"<Pending>"`.

svg-focusable.description: Reports an `<svg>` that has no `focusable` attribute.

syntax-specified.description: Reports a file without `syntax = ...;` or `edition = ...;`, which makes it proto2.

table-scope.description: Reports a `scope` attribute on an element other than `<th>`.

test-and-or.description: Reports a `[ ]` test that joins conditions with `-a` or `-o`.

test-exit-status.description: Reports a test that compares `$?` with a number, as in `[ $? -eq 0 ]`.

test-grep-output.description: Reports a `[[ ]]` or `[ -n ]` / `[ -z ]` test of the output of a pipeline or command that ends in `grep`.

test-negated-empty.description: Reports a test that negates `-z` or `-n`, as in `[ ! -z "$x" ]`.

text-content.description: Reports a `<button>` with no name: no text (an `<svg>` counts by the text inside it, such as its `<title>`), no image with a non-empty `alt` and no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

timestamp-expanded.description: Reports a variable whose value runs `date` and that is not simply expanded (`:=`, `::=`): every use runs `date` again and the values differ within one build.

todo-comment.description: Reports a line of a comment that starts with `todo` in any other case, or with `TODO` and no colon.

trailing-comma-on-call-site.description: Reports the last argument of a multi-line call that has a trailing comma the formatter would add or remove.

trailing-comma-on-declaration-site.description: Reports the last parameter of a multi-line declaration that has a trailing comma the formatter would add or remove.

trap-expands-now.description: Reports a `trap` whose command is double-quoted and contains an expansion, as in `trap "rm $tmp" EXIT`.

triple-slash-reference.description: Reports a `/// <reference path="x" />` or `/// <reference types="x" />` before the first statement of the file; for `types` only when the file also imports that module.

tuple-element-names-in-signatures.description: Reports a tuple type in the signature of a method, constructor, property, indexer, conversion operator or delegate whose elements have no names.

type-alias-annotation.description: Reports `X: TypeAlias = ...` when the `target_version` has the `type` statement (3.12 and later).

type-case.description: Reports a data type name not in the case that the `policy` option sets.

policy.description: The case the words must be in: `consistent` follows the first one written.

type-check-without-type-error.description: Reports a branch tested with `isinstance`, `issubclass` or `callable` that raises a builtin exception other than `TypeError` (`NotImplementedError` is accepted too).

type-comparison.description: Reports a comparison with `==` or `!=` where one side is `type(x)` or a builtin class such as `int`.

type-var-name-variance.description: Reports a `TypeVar` with `covariant=True` whose name does not end in `_co`, or with `contravariant=True` and a name that does not end in `_contra`.

typed-variables.description: Reports a `variable` block with no `type` argument.

unassigned-variable.description: Reports a lower case variable that the file reads and never assigns, reads with `read`, `getopts`, `local` or a `for` loop, or guards with a default (`${name:-x}`).

undefined-export.description: Reports a name in `__all__` that the module does not bind.

undefined-local-with-import-star-usage.description: Reports a name that no scope binds in a file that has a star import.

undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-.description: Reports a star import in a function or class.

undefined-variable.description: Reports a name that no scope declares, that is not a global of ES2026 (or, in a `.cjs` file, `require`, `module`, `exports` and `global`) and that is not in the option `globals`.

globals.description: Names the environment declares (ESLint's `languageOptions.globals`), such as `window` or `console`.

underscore-prefixed-variable-used.description: Reports a variable whose name starts with `_`, which says it is unused, but that is read.

unicode-literal.description: Reports a string with the `u` prefix.

union-annotation.description: Reports a `typing.Union[...]` subscript when the `target_version` has `X | Y` (3.10 and later).

union-distinct.description: Reports a `UNION` that names neither `DISTINCT` nor `ALL`.

unique-fragment-name.description: Reports two fragments of a document with the same name, within one file.

unique-landmark.description: Reports landmarks of the same kind (`<nav>`, `<aside>`, or elements with the same landmark `role`) that a screen reader user cannot tell apart: with several of them, each needs an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` that no other has.

unique-operation-name.description: Reports two operations of a document with the same name, within one file.

unique-targets.description: Reports a target defined by more than one rule, which merges prerequisites and overrides recipes.

ignore.description: Targets that may be defined more than once.

unit-allowed-list.description: Reports a unit (`%` included) that is not in the `list` option, in values and at-rule preludes.

unit-disallowed-list.description: Reports a unit (`%` included) that is in the `list` option, in values and at-rule preludes.

unit-no-unknown.description: Reports a unit that is not a CSS unit, in values and `@media` preludes.

unknown-columns.description: Reports a wildcard of the outermost query that resolves to a table: a `*` over a table, or over a subquery or common table that has one itself.

unknown-needs.description: Reports a `needs` entry that names a job that the workflow does not define.

unknown-property.description: Reports a property name that is not an EditorConfig or .NET property (`dotnet_*`, `csharp_*`, `visual_basic_*`, naming rules, `dotnet_diagnostic.<ID>.severity`) but is one typo away from one.

strict.description: Also report `dotnet_*`, `csharp_*` and `visual_basic_*` names that are close to no known property (the list may lag behind new .NET options).

unknown-rule-in-directive.description: Reports a comment that disables rules of another tool (`# rubocop:disable Foo/Bar`) by a `Group/Name` whose group the tool does not have, for example the group of an extension that is not installed.

unnecessary-collection-call.description: Reports `dict()`, `list()` or `tuple()` with no arguments, and `dict(a=1)` with only keyword arguments.

unnecessary-placeholder.description: Reports a `pass` or `...` statement in a body that has two statements or more.

unqualified-reference.description: Reports a column reference without a table in a select over more than one table or view.

unquoted-pattern.description: Reports a `==`, `!=` or `=` in `[[ ]]` whose right side is an unquoted expansion.

unreachable-code.description: Reports a statement that can never run: after `return`, `throw`, `break` or `continue`, after an `if`/`else` or `try` that always jumps, or after a loop that never ends.

non_returning_calls.description: With a flow layer, treat the code after a call that never returns (`[DoesNotReturn]`, `does_not_return` in `semantics:`) as unreachable. A compiler does not, so turn this off to report exactly what it reports.

unrecognized-char-ref.description: Reports a named character reference in text (`&name;`) that HTML does not define.

unsafe-new-static.description: Reports `new static` in a class that is not final and has no final or abstract constructor of its own.

unsafe-numbers.description: Reports a number that a double-precision parser (JavaScript and most JSON libraries) cannot hold exactly: an integer beyond 2^53 - 1, a value that overflows to infinity, or one that underflows to zero or is subnormal.

unset-glob.description: Reports `unset name[i]` with an unquoted subscript.

unsorted-dunder-all.description: Reports an `__all__` list or tuple of strings that is out of order: constants (upper case) first, then classes (capitalized), then the rest, each group in natural order.

unsorted-dunder-slots.description: Reports a `__slots__` list or tuple of strings that is not in natural order.

unsorted-imports.description: Reports a block of imports that differs from the sorted layout.

force_sort_within_sections.description: Sort `import x` and `from x import y` together by module instead of the plain imports first.

line_width.description: A `from` import over this many columns is wrapped in parentheses, one member to a line.

sections.description: The sections of the block in the order they are written; a section left out comes last.

untagged-base-image.description: Reports a `FROM` image with neither a tag nor a digest (`FROM alpine`).

unused-alias.description: Reports a table alias in a `FROM` clause that no qualified reference of the select, nested queries included, uses.

unused-annotation.description: Reports a local variable that is annotated without a value and never read.

unused-assignment.description: Reports a value stored in a local variable that no path reads before it is overwritten or the variable goes out of scope (a dead store).

unused-block-argument.description: Reports a block parameter that the block never reads.

unused-cte.description: Reports a common table expression that nothing in the `WITH` statement refers to.

unused-declarations.description: Reports a variable, local value, data source or provider alias that no file of the module (the `.tf` files of the directory) refers to.

unused-import.description: Reports an import whose name the file does not use.

unused-local-variable.description: Reports a local variable that is declared, and perhaps assigned, but never read.

unused-method-argument.description: Reports a method parameter that the method never reads.

unused-parameter.description: Reports a parameter of a function with a body (a declaration or a literal) that its body never mentions.

args.description: Which parameters are checked: those after the last one that is read, all of them, or none.

ignore_pattern.description: A regex for the names that are not checked (revive's `allowRegex`).

unused-private-member.description: Reports a private field, method, property or event that no file of the project uses (needs `analysis: deep`).

reflection_base_types.description: Names of base classes whose derived types are called by a framework                           through reflection (with `reflection_methods`). A base is matched by its                           simple name anywhere up the inheritance chain, also when the project                           does not load its assembly.

reflection_methods.description: Names of private methods that count as used in a type derived from                           one of `reflection_base_types`.

unused-unpacked-variable.description: Reports a name of a tuple target in a function that the function never reads.

unused-variable.description: Reports a local variable or catch variable that is never used, or that is only assigned constants and never read.

upper-ell.description: Reports an integer literal that ends in a lower case `l` (`10l`).

use-baseline.description: Reports an element, an attribute or an attribute value that not all major browsers support (`<geolocation>`, `popover="hint"`, `rel="manifest"` on `<link>`), by the baseline data of web-features.

available.description: How widely a feature must be available: `widely` (in all major browsers for 30 months), `newly` (in all of them), or a year (baseline since that year or before).

use-before-define.description: Reports a reference that comes before the declaration of what it names in the source (function declarations included), or that runs while the variable is being initialized.

use-isnan.description: Reports a comparison with `NaN` (`NaN` or `Number.NaN` on either side of `==`, `!=`, `===`, `!==`, `<`, `>`...), and `NaN` as the `switch` discriminant or as a `case` test.

use-lambda.description: Reports an anonymous method (`delegate (x) { ... }`) where a lambda can be written.

use-literal-suffix.description: Reports a numeric literal cast to `long`, `ulong`, `uint`, `float`, `double` or `decimal` when the literal's own type differs: `(long)1` is `1L`.

use-tuple-syntax.description: Reports `ValueTuple<int, int>` and `ValueTuple.Create(a, b)` where tuple syntax (`(int, int)` and `(a, b)`) can be used; not inside an expression tree.

use-workdir-not-cd.description: Reports a `RUN` that calls `cd`, anywhere in its script (also in a subshell such as `(cd sub && make)`).

useless-access-modifier.description: Reports a bare `private`, `protected`, `public` or `module_function` that repeats the visibility already in force, or is followed by no method definition.

useless-cat.description: Reports a pipeline that starts with `cat file`.

useless-echo.description: Reports an `echo` whose only argument is a command substitution, as in `echo $(cmd)`.

useless-import-alias.description: Reports `import a as a` and `from m import a as a`.

useless-method-definition.description: Reports a method whose whole body is a bare `super`.

useless-object-inheritance.description: Reports a class that has the builtin `object` as a base.

useless-semicolon.description: Reports a `;` at the end of a line.

using-order.description: Reports `using` directives of a file or namespace that are out of order: `System` first (`system_first`), names in alphabetical order (`compare`), and, with the options `static_position` and `alias_position` set to `after`, `using static` directives after the plain ones and aliases after those, each group sorted.

alias_position.description: `after`: alias directives come after all other usings, sorted by alias name; `keep`: they stay where they are.

compare.description: `ordinal` compares code points; `culture` ignores case (and puts punctuation before digits before letters, a lower-case name before an upper-case one that is otherwise equal); `culture_ignore_case` leaves names that differ only in case in their order.

static_position.description: `after`: `using static` directives come after the plain usings, sorted (System ones first with `system_first`); `keep`: they stay where they are.

system_first.description: Put `System` and `System.*` before the other namespaces.

using-placement.description: Reports a `using` directive outside the namespace declaration in a file that has one.

v-bind-style.description: Reports `v-bind:` where the shorthand `:` would do (`v-bind:href`).

v-on-event-hyphenation.description: Reports an event of a component that is written in camelCase (`@cardOpen`).

v-on-style.description: Reports `v-on:` where the shorthand `@` would do (`v-on:click`).

v-slot-style.description: Reports `v-slot:` where the shorthand `#` would do (`v-slot:head`).

valid-id.description: Reports an `id` that is empty, has white space, begins with a digit or has characters other than letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

valid-typeof.description: Reports a `typeof` comparison whose other side is a string that `typeof` never returns (a typo such as `'strnig'`, or `'null'`), or the identifier `undefined` instead of the string `'undefined'`.

valid-v-bind.description: Reports a `v-bind` that has no expression (`:name` alone is the shorthand for `:name="name"`, a bare `v-bind` is not) or a modifier other than `camel`, `prop`, `attr` and `sync`.

valid-v-cloak.description: Reports a `v-cloak` that has an expression, an argument or a modifier.

valid-v-else.description: Reports a `v-else` that has an expression, an argument or a modifier, shares an element with `v-if` or `v-else-if`, or is not on the element right after one with `v-if` or `v-else-if`.

valid-v-else-if.description: Reports a `v-else-if` that has no expression, has an argument or a modifier, shares an element with `v-if` or `v-else`, or is not on the element right after one with `v-if` or `v-else-if`.

valid-v-for.description: Reports a `v-for` whose value is not `item in items` (or `of`), or that has an argument or a modifier.

valid-v-html.description: Reports a `v-html` that has no expression, an argument or a modifier.

valid-v-if.description: Reports a `v-if` that has no expression, has an argument or a modifier, or is on the same element as `v-else` or `v-else-if`.

valid-v-is.description: Reports a `v-is` that has no expression, an argument or a modifier.

valid-v-memo.description: Reports a `v-memo` that has no expression, an argument or a modifier.

valid-v-model.description: Reports a `v-model` that has no expression, and a `v-model` on a file input.

valid-v-on.description: Reports a `v-on` with no handler and no modifier (`@click`).

valid-v-once.description: Reports a `v-once` that has an expression, an argument or a modifier.

valid-v-pre.description: Reports a `v-pre` that has an expression, an argument or a modifier.

valid-v-show.description: Reports a `v-show` that has no expression, an argument or a modifier.

valid-v-slot.description: Reports a `v-slot` with a modifier, and a `v-slot` on a plain HTML element (`<div #item>`).

valid-v-text.description: Reports a `v-text` that has no expression, an argument or a modifier.

value-no-vendor-prefix.description: Reports a vendor-prefixed keyword or function that has a standard value (`-webkit-flex`).

var-naming.description: Reports a name that is not spelled in Go style: it has an underscore, it is a constant in ALL_CAPS, or it writes a common initialism (`Id`, `Http`, `Url`) in mixed case.

ignore_pattern.description: A regex for the names that are not checked.

initialisms.description: The words (in capitals) that are written in capitals inside a name.

names.description: The convention of the names: `words` or `off`.

verbose-raise.description: Reports `raise e` in an `except ... as e` clause.

void-style.description:
Reports a `/` at the end of a void element (`
`, ``).

wget-progress.description: Reports a `wget` call that does not limit its progress output.

when-entry-bracing.description: Reports a `when` entry whose first line the formatter would change.

workdir-absolute.description: Reports a `WORKDIR` with a relative path.

workflow-syntax.description: Reports a key that a section does not have, a required key or section that is missing, a section of the wrong kind (a list where a map is needed), or an empty one.

yield-outside-function.description: Reports a `yield`, `yield from` or `await` outside a function.

yum-clean.description: Reports a `RUN` that installs with yum and does not clean the cache.

yum-yes.description: Reports a `yum install`, `yum groupinstall` or `yum localinstall` without `-y` or `--assumeyes`.

zip-without-explicit-strict.description: Reports a call of `zip` with several arguments (or a starred one) and no `strict` keyword, for a `target_version` of 3.10 and later.

zypper-clean.description: Reports a `RUN` that installs with zypper and does not clean the cache.

zypper-pin-versions.description: Reports a `zypper install` (`in`) of a package without a version.

zypper-yes.description: Reports a `zypper` command that asks for confirmation.

description: Configuration of Sudsy, the formatter and linter for source and data files.

analysis.description: Analysis depth for rules: fast (syntax only), standard (within each file), deep (adds project scope).

bracket_same_line.description: Put the `>` of a multi-line start tag at the end of the last attribute's line.

content_newline_with_attributes.description: Put the content of an element that has attributes on lines of its own, also when the element fits on a line; inline elements and `pre` keep theirs (`vue/singleline-html-element-content-newline` with its defaults).

content_newline_with_elements.description: Put the children of an element that has an element child on lines of their own, also when they fit on a line; only where the whitespace between them is not significant (`whitespace_sensitivity: ignore`, `@html-eslint/element-newline`).

embedded_language_formatting.description: Format the code of `<script>` and `<style>` and of `style`, `srcset` and event-handler attributes with the formatter of its language (`auto`, Prettier's `embeddedLanguageFormatting`), or keep it as written (`off`). Code that does not parse, or of a language that is not installed, is kept either way.

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

indent_comment_lines.description: Put the lines of a multi-line comment one level deeper than the comment and a closing `-->` on a line of its own at the comment's level, whatever indentation they had (`@html-eslint/indent`); the default keeps them as written.

indent_expression_operands.description: Indent the operands of a binary or logical expression that continues on following lines in an attribute or `{{ }}` expression (`vue/html-indent`); the default aligns them with the first operand.

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

max_attributes_per_line.description: Put every attribute of a start tag that has more than this many on its own line (`vue/max-attributes-per-line`, `@html-eslint/attrs-newline`); 0 sets no limit. `single_attribute_per_line` is the limit 1.

self_closing_space.description:
Write a space before the `/>` of a self-closing element (``, `
`); off writes `` (`@html-eslint/no-extra-spacing-tags`).

single_attribute_per_line.description: Put every attribute of a tag that has several on its own line.

void_element_style.description:
How a void element (`br`, `img`, ...) is written: `selfclose` as `
`, `omit` as `
` (`void-style`).

whitespace_sensitivity.description: Whether whitespace between inline elements and text is significant: `css` follows each element's CSS display, `strict` treats every element as inline, `ignore` as block.

semantics.description: Facts about methods that the flow analyses use.

does_not_return.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

pure.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

access_modifier_outdent.description: Columns `public:`, `private:` and `protected:` are outdented from the members of their class.

align_after_open_bracket.description: Wrapped lines inside brackets line up with the first token after the bracket (`align`), continue with `continuation_indent` (`dont_align`), or always start on a new line after the bracket (`always_break`).

align_escaped_newlines.description: The backslashes of a multi-line macro: aligned at `line_width` (`right`), one blank after the longest line (`left`) or one blank after each line.

align_trailing_comments.description: Align the trailing comments of consecutive lines.

align_with_tabs.description: With `indent_style: tab`, the alignment of continuation lines uses tabs for each whole indent width and spaces for the rest.

bin_pack_arguments.description: Call arguments that do not fit on a line are filled; when false they go one per line (or all on one line).

bin_pack_parameters.description: Function parameters that do not fit on a line are filled; when false they go one per line (or all on one line).

brace_wrapping.description: Constructs whose opening brace goes on its own line: `class`, `struct`, `union`, `enum`, `function`, `namespace`, `extern`, `control` (if, for, while, switch, do, try), `case`, `else` (the `else` after a block starts a line), `catch` (the `catch` after a block starts a line), `while` (the `while` of a do loop starts a line). Empty: every brace stays on the line of its construct.

braced_list_padding.description: A blank inside the braces of an initializer list (`{ 1, 2 }` against `{1, 2}`); an empty list is `{}`.

break_after_return_type.description: The function name goes on a new line after its return type: never, for declarations and definitions outside classes (`top_level`), for all, or for definitions only (`top_level_definitions`, `all_definitions`).

break_before_binary_operators.description: A wrapped binary expression breaks after the operator (`none`), before it except for assignments (`non_assignment`) or before every operator (`all`).

break_constructor_initializers.description: Constructor initializer lists that do not fit start on a new line before the colon (`before_colon`, one initializer per line when needed), or put a comma before each initializer, one per line (`before_comma`).

break_template_declarations.description: `template <...>` ends its line: always (`yes`), when the declaration is not on one line (`multiline`) or never.

collapse_empty_blocks.description: An empty body is `{}` when its line fits, except the block of `if`, `for`, `while`, `do`, `try` and `catch` and a block inside a block, which has two lines (`if (x) {\n}`).

comment_keep_unicode_blanks.description: A comment loses only trailing ASCII whitespace; a no-break space at its end stays.

constructor_initializer_indent.description: Columns a constructor initializer list is indented more than its constructor.

continuation_indent.description: Columns a wrapped line is indented more than the line it continues, where it is not aligned to a bracket.

derive_pointer_alignment.description: Take `pointer_alignment` from the file: the side that most of its declarators of pointers and references use (a `*` or `&` with a blank before and none after against none before and a blank after); `pointer_alignment` stays where both sides are equal.

empty_body_own_line.description: The `;` that is the whole body of an `if`, `for` or `while` goes on its own line below the head, indented (`while (x)\n  ;`).

empty_line_before_access_modifier.description: A blank line before `public:`, `private:` and `protected:` (not the first item of a class): removed (`never`), as written (`leave`), added unless a comment stands in front (`logical_block`) or always added.

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

for_each_macros.description: Names of macros that are used as loops: `name(args) {` is a `control` brace. Any other `name(args) {` is a function definition for `brace_wrapping`.

indent_braces.description: Indent a brace that is on its own line together with the block it opens.

indent_case_labels.description: Indent `case` labels one level inside their `switch`.

indent_goto_labels.description: A goto label stands one indent left of the statements of its block; when false it starts at column 0.

indent_pp_directives.description: A preprocessor directive starts with `#` directly followed by its keyword (`none`) or keeps the blanks written after the `#` (`keep`).

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

join_closing_angles.description: Two closing template brackets are written together (`A<B<C>>` against `A<B<C> >`), as C++11 reads them. Only a `>` that closes a template bracket is joined, a comparison or a shift stays apart.

keep_blank_lines_at_end_of_blocks.description: A blank line before the closing brace of a block stays.

keep_leading_blank_lines.description: Blank lines at the start of the file stay.

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

max_blank_lines.description: Largest number of blank lines kept between statements and comments.

namespace_indentation.description: Indent the contents of namespaces: `none`, only namespaces nested in another (`inner`), or `all`.

penalty_return_type.description: What a return type on a line of its own costs the layout; the higher, the longer the parameter list may wrap before the return type moves.

pointer_alignment.description: Where the `*` and `&` of a pointer or reference declarator go: next to the name (`right`), next to the type (`left`) or between them (`middle`).

pointer_qualifier_words.description: Words that are no name when they follow a `*`, `&` or `&&` of a declarator (`T &noexcept`): a blank stands before them.

short_case_labels.description: A `case` label and its simple statement are kept on one line when they fit.

short_enums.description: An enum whose body fits stays on one line.

short_functions.description: Function bodies kept on the line of the signature when they fit: `none`, `empty` (`{}` only), `inline` (functions defined in a class, and empty ones) or `all`.

short_ifs.description: An `if` with a simple statement is kept on one line when it fits: `never`, without an `else`, or with or without.

short_lambdas.description: Lambda bodies kept on the line of the lambda when they fit: `none`, `empty`, `inline` (a lambda that is an argument) or `all`.

short_loops.description: A `for`, `while` or range-for with a simple statement is kept on one line when it fits.

space_after_cast.description: A blank after the `)` of a C cast (`(int) x` against `(int)x`).

space_before_parens.description: A blank before the parenthesis of `if`, `for`, `while`, `switch` and `catch` (`control_statements`), before every parenthesis (`always`) or never.

spaces_before_trailing_comments.description: Blanks between the code of a line and its `//` comment.

split_empty_braces.description: Words of `brace_wrapping` whose empty body keeps `{` and `}` on two lines when the `{` is on its own line (`void f()\n{\n}`), as `SplitEmptyFunction`, `SplitEmptyRecord` and `SplitEmptyNamespace`. Other empty bodies are `{}`.

wrap_lines.description: Break lines that are longer than `line_width`. When false, every line keeps the line breaks of the source (only indentation and spacing change).

semantics.description: Facts about methods that the flow analyses use.

does_not_return.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

pure.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

leading_argument_commands.description: Commands whose first argument stays on the line of the command when the call breaks (`set(NAME` then the values).

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

max_blank_lines.description: Largest number of blank lines kept between commands and comments.
